ai.description: This frog reaches 5–7 cm. It is olive-brown with dark dorsal spots and a pale belly. Distinctive features include a broad, flattened head and extensively webbed toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Allopaa hazarensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, glandular, horseshoe-shaped fold on the chest, which is absent in other similar *Paa* species.
ai.habitat: The Kashmir Paa Frog inhabits high-altitude streams and rocky mountain torrents in the Himalayas, typically found between 1,000 and 2,500 meters amidst sparse vegetation.
ai.behavior: The Kashmir Paa frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the rocky banks of fast-flowing mountain streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Allopaa hazarensis* is an oviparous frog that breeds from May to August, laying clutches of eggs in rocky mountain streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Allopaa hazarensis* is found in the western Himalayas, specifically within Jammu and Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh, at elevations ranging from 1,000 to 2,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Allopaa hazarensis* consists of a series of low-pitched, rhythmic pulses produced by males while submerged in fast-flowing mountain streams.
